# Through Their Eyes — synthetic match dataset (v1)

A datasheet in the style of Gebru et al., *Datasheets for Datasets* (Communications of the ACM
64(12), 2021). Repository: https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes (links below
point there, so they also work from the copy of this file inside the archive).

**Every match, team and player in this dataset is synthetic and fictional.** It was generated by
our simulator. It contains no real match data, and nothing in it is a finding about real football.

At a glance (v1, built on macOS arm64):

| | |
|---|---|
| Matches | 10 stitched matches, match seeds 5001–5010 |
| Play | 130.5 min in all; 12:25–13:28 per match; 19 possessions each |
| Frames | 195,793 at 25 Hz; 4,307,446 player rows |
| Events | 101,202: 61,730 scans, 31,176 head turns, 2,714 passes, 2,089 receptions, 515 interceptions, 516 possession changes, 2,228 pressure spells, 190 restarts, 14 balls out of play, 10 shots, 10 keeper dives, 9 goals, 1 tackle |
| Perception | 2,089 receptions, each with the receiver's scans in the 10 s before it and his belief about all 21 other players (43,869 rows) |
| Decisions | 30 decisions on belief, with all 339 options weighed |
| Archive | `through-their-eyes-synthetic-matches-v1.tar.gz`, about 70 MB |
| Licence | **TODO(Bowen):** proposed CC BY 4.0 for the data; the code stays MIT ([§ Licence](#licence)) |

A one-possession sample of the same files (under 200 KB) is in the repository:
[`data/sample/`](https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes/tree/main/data/sample).
A worked example that reads the files:
[`examples/dataset_quickstart.py`](https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes/blob/main/examples/dataset_quickstart.py).

## Motivation

- **Why it exists.** Public tracking data rarely records where a player looked or what he knew.
  Our simulator records both: every scan as a ground-truth event, and every player's belief about
  every other player. This dataset packages its output so that others can test perception
  analytics against that ground truth: scan detectors, vision and pressing metrics, belief
  models. Head yaw comes both as tracked, with sensor noise, and as true.
- **Who made it.** It was built for the Microsoft × Premier League "Inside the Game" hackathon
  (2026), whose brief asks for synthetic, football-realistic datasets with events such as passes,
  shots, tackles, possession changes, pressure events and match metadata.

## Composition

- **Instances.** A match is 19 possessions on one clock. 15 are open-play passages
  (`possession_play`), each until the ball goes out or a fixed cap of 30–70 s. Four are scripted
  hero scenarios: `blind_side_run`, `press_escape`, `far_post_finish` and `corner_blind_side`
  (sim/README.md). The layout is `sim.dataset.LAYOUT`. Each possession is simulated on its own
  and placed after the previous one (SPEC 3.1).
- **Players.** The same 22 fictional players play every match: home H1–H11 (4-3-3) and away
  A1–A11 (4-2-3-1). Names come from `sim/roster.py`. Each player's sim parameters are in
  `metadata.json`.
- **Teams.** "Home" and "Away". There are no club names, crests or kits in the data.
- **Labels.** Scans are ground truth (`scan` events). Partial head turns that are not scans are
  `head_turn` events. Beliefs and decisions are the sim's own state, not annotations.
- **Missing values.** These columns are null by design:
  - `events.x`/`y` for events without a location (scans, head turns, dives, possession changes);
  - `outcome` and `end_*` of 93 passes still rolling when their possession was cut;
  - `ball.owner` while the ball is free;
  - `decisions.target_player` for carries and shots.
- **Splits.** None. Every match is generated the same way, from fresh seeds.
- **Relationships.** Every table has `match_id` (the match seed) and a match `frame`.
  - `event_id` joins `events`, `receptions` and `beliefs`.
  - `metadata.json` lists each match's possessions; `possession` indexes them.
  - `tracking` and `ball` are aligned frame by frame.
- **Sensitive data.** None. Nothing in it relates to a real person.

### Conventions

- SI units. Positions are in metres on a 105 × 68 m pitch, with the origin at the centre spot.
  The home team attacks the goal at +x in every possession.
- Frames run at 25 Hz from 0 at the first kick-off; `t` = frame / 25 s. Frames are continuous
  across possessions.
- Angles are in radians, counter-clockwise from +x, wrapped to [−π, π].
- Positions and velocities are quantised to 1 mm and 1 mm/s, angles to 1e-4 rad (SPEC 3.7).
  Tracking stores them as float32.
- Event ids are `<type>:<player>:<frame>`.

### `events`

`events.csv` and `events.parquet` hold the same rows, ordered by `match_id`, `frame` and
`event_id`.

| Column | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_id` | int32 | | match seed; joins `metadata.json` `matches[].match_id` |
| `event_id` | string | | `<type>:<player>:<frame>`, unique within a match |
| `type` | string | | one of the event types below |
| `source` | string | | `sim`: emitted by the engine; `stitch`: a restart; `derived`: computed from tracking |
| `possession` | int32 | | index of the possession in its match |
| `frame` | int32 | frame | when it happened (scans and head turns: onset) |
| `t` | float64 | s | frame / 25 |
| `player` | string | | the actor (see below) |
| `team` | int8 | | the actor's team: 0 home, 1 away |
| `x` | float64 | m | where it happened (see below) |
| `y` | float64 | m | |
| `end_frame` | int32 | frame | a pass or shot resolved, a scan or head turn over, a pressure spell's last frame |
| `end_x` | float64 | m | ball position when a pass or shot was resolved |
| `end_y` | float64 | m | |
| `outcome` | string | | pass: `complete`, `intercepted`, `out` or `offside`; shot: `goal`, `saved`, `wide`, `blocked` or `post` (back into play off the woodwork) |
| `recipient` | string | | pass: the teammate it was played to |
| `receiver` | string | | pass: who controlled it, teammate or interceptor; null when it went out |
| `attrs` | string | | every attribute the sim recorded for the event, as JSON (frames in match time) |

Event types:

| `type` | `source` | `player` | `x`, `y` | Notable `attrs` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pass` | sim | passer | ball at the kick | `to`, `target` (aim point, m), `speed` (launch speed, m/s), `distance` (m), `receiver`, `end`, `end_at` |
| `reception` | sim | a teammate of the passer who controls the ball | ball | `at` |
| `interception` | sim | an opponent who controls the free ball | ball | `at` |
| `possession_change` | sim | who won the ball (interception or tackle), same frame | — | |
| `tackle` | sim | the tackler; only `press_escape` has tackles | ball | `won_from`, `at` |
| `out` | sim | the last player to touch it | ball on the first frame the whole ball is off the pitch (Law 9) | `at`, `line` (`touchline` or `goal_line`) |
| `shot` | sim | shooter | ball at the strike | `placement` (near or far post), `aim`, `speed` (m/s), `error` (aim error, rad), `keeper`, `goal_line_y` (m), `seen` (the keeper's first sight of the ball, frame), `reach` (m), `p_save`, `outcome` |
| `dive` | sim | goalkeeper | — | `toward` (m), `seen` (frame) |
| `save` | sim | goalkeeper | ball | `shot` (event id) |
| `goal` | sim | the last player to touch it; `team` is the scoring team | ball on the first frame the whole ball is past the goal line, between the posts (Law 10) | `at`, `line`, `own_goal` (true for an own goal) |
| `offside` | sim | the player in an offside position who became involved (Law 11) | — | `at` (where; the defenders' indirect free kick), `how`, `kick` (the pass's event id), `kick_frame`, `margin` (m beyond the line), `line` (who set it), `awarded_to` |
| `post` | sim | the last player to kick it | — | `at` (where the ball met the post) |
| `scan` | sim | the player | — | `direction` (world yaw he turned to, rad), `amplitude` (rad from the ball), `key` (the hero scenario's key scan) |
| `head_turn` | sim | the player | — | a partial turn away and straight back, not a scan: `direction`, `amplitude`, `partial` |
| `restart` | stitch | the possession's first carrier | ball at its first frame | `kind`: `kick_off`, `throw_in`, `goal_kick`, `corner`, `free_kick` (after offside) or `cut`; `scenario` |
| `pressure` | derived | the main presser | the carrier at the start | `carrier`, `peak`, `peak_frame`, `threshold` |

- **How a restart's `kind` is set.** The first possession, and one after a goal, kick off. A
  set-piece scenario starts with its own set piece. Otherwise `kind` says how the *previous*
  possession stopped: where the ball went out, `free_kick` after an offside call, or `cut` when
  it was still in play. The next
  possession then starts from its own scripted set-up (SPEC 3.1). See the limitations.
- **How a `pressure` spell is defined.** We compute it; the sim emits no pressure events.
  - It is a run of frames with one ball carrier whose pressing intensity is at least 0.7.
  - Pressing intensity follows Bekkers (2025), as `analytics/pressing.py` computes it.
  - 0.7 is the explain layer's threshold for "under heavy pressure" (`explain/lexicon.py`).
  - The main presser is the defender with the highest intensity on the carrier at the peak.
  - Spells are short: median 0.12 s, and 28% last a single frame. In open play the closest
    opponent stops 3 m from the carrier, so the intensity hovers near the threshold. Filter by
    `end_frame − frame` if you need sustained pressure.

### `tracking`

`tracking.parquet`: one row per player per frame, ordered by `match_id`, `frame` and the player
order of `metadata.json`.

| Column | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_id` | int32 | | match seed |
| `frame` | int32 | frame | match frame |
| `possession` | int32 | | possession index |
| `player` | string | | player id |
| `team` | int8 | | 0 home, 1 away |
| `x` | float32 | m | position |
| `y` | float32 | m | position |
| `vx` | float32 | m/s | velocity |
| `vy` | float32 | m/s | velocity |
| `body_yaw` | float32 | rad | body orientation |
| `head_yaw` | float32 | rad | head orientation as a tracking system would report it, with Gaussian sensor noise (σ = 2°) |
| `head_yaw_true` | float32 | rad | the head orientation he saw with |
| `has_ball` | bool | | he controls the ball this frame |

### `ball`

`ball.parquet`: one row per frame.

| Column | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_id` | int32 | | match seed |
| `frame` | int32 | frame | match frame |
| `possession` | int32 | | possession index |
| `x` | float32 | m | position |
| `y` | float32 | m | position |
| `z` | float32 | m | height of the ball's centre; always 0.11 m (its radius), as there is no aerial play |
| `vx` | float32 | m/s | velocity |
| `vy` | float32 | m/s | velocity |
| `vz` | float32 | m/s | velocity; always 0 |
| `owner` | string | | the player who controls it; null while it is free |

### `receptions`

`receptions.csv` and `receptions.parquet`: one row per `reception` event.

| Column | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_id` | int32 | | match seed |
| `event_id` | string | | the reception event |
| `frame` | int32 | frame | reception frame |
| `possession` | int32 | | possession index |
| `player` | string | | the receiver |
| `team` | int8 | | 0 home, 1 away |
| `role` | string | | the receiver's role |
| `scans` | int32 | | his scans that began in the window (`scan` events; head turns do not count) |
| `window_s` | float64 | s | 10 s before the reception, cut to the start of his team's spell on the ball or of the possession, as `eval/realism.py` counts (Jordet et al. 2013, 2020) |
| `belief_error_teammates_m` | float64 | m | mean distance from believed to true position, over his teammates |
| `belief_error_opponents_m` | float64 | m | the same over the opponents |
| `belief_error_max_m` | float64 | m | the largest over all 21 |

In v1 a receiver scans 2.98 times on average, in a mean window of 7.4 s.

### `beliefs`

`beliefs.parquet`: at every reception, the receiver's belief about each of the 21 other players.

This is the sim's belief store (SPEC 3.4). A player sees whoever has visibility ≥ 0.5 from his
true head yaw. For everyone he keeps the last sighting's position and velocity, extrapolated at
most 1 s. It is rebuilt from the tracking by `sim.dataset.BeliefReplay`, after the receiver
perceives the reception frame. The replay reproduces the sim's own belief at every decision
exactly (`tests/test_dataset.py`). Every possession starts with everyone seen at its first frame.

| Column | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_id` | int32 | | match seed |
| `event_id` | string | | the reception event |
| `frame` | int32 | frame | reception frame |
| `observer` | string | | the receiver, whose belief this is |
| `target` | string | | the player he holds a belief about |
| `believed_x` | float64 | m | where he believes the target is |
| `believed_y` | float64 | m | |
| `true_x` | float64 | m | where the target is |
| `true_y` | float64 | m | |
| `error_m` | float64 | m | distance from believed to true position |
| `age_s` | float64 | s | time since he last saw the target; 0 when in sight |

### `decisions`

`decisions.csv` and `decisions.parquet`: one row per option a ball carrier weighed (SPEC 3.5).

Only the hero scenarios' carriers decide. Open-play passes follow a rule (below), so v1 has three
decisions per match.

| Column | Type | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match_id` | int32 | | match seed |
| `frame` | int32 | frame | decision frame: 0.2 s after he took control, or when his carry ended |
| `possession` | int32 | | possession index |
| `player` | string | | the ball carrier deciding |
| `action` | string | | `pass:<id>`, `carry`, `shot:near` or `shot:far` |
| `kind` | string | | `pass`, `carry` or `shot` |
| `target_player` | string | | pass: the teammate |
| `target_x` | float64 | m | where the action aims |
| `target_y` | float64 | m | |
| `p_success` | float64 | | P(success), on his belief |
| `value` | float64 | xT | expected threat after the action, on his belief (a smooth xT prior, SPEC 3.5) |
| `prob` | float64 | | softmax probability of choosing it |
| `noise` | float64 | | the keyed Gumbel noise of the choice: he takes argmax(value / T + noise) (Oberst & Sontag 2019) |
| `chosen` | bool | | the option he took |

### `metadata.json`

- `teams`.
- `players`: id, team, shirt number, role and fictional name. Also each player's sim parameters:
  - `v_max_mps`, `a_max_mps2`, `d_max_mps2`: speed, acceleration and deceleration limits;
  - `scan_rate_hz`: the spontaneous scan rate while his head is free and no opponent is within
    10 m; measured rates are lower;
  - `decision_temperature`: the softmax temperature.
- `pitch`, `units` and `frame_rate_hz`.
- `matches`: per match, frames, duration and score. Per possession:
  - `scenario`, its `seed` and `start_frame`;
  - `restart`, `first_team` (the team on the ball at its first frame) and `score_before`;
  - `hero`: the scenario's hero, or null.

`manifest.json` lists every file with its size, SHA-256 and row count, and the Python, numpy and
pyarrow versions and the platform it was built with.

## Generation process

- **Engine.** A numpy simulator at 25 Hz (`sim/`; [SPEC 3](https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md#3-synthetic-match-engine-sim)).
  Each step runs, in order:
  1. perception;
  2. scripted actions and due decisions;
  3. heads and scans;
  4. movement with speed and acceleration limits;
  5. the ball: rolling resistance and drag, control, interception, out of play.
- **Seeds.** Every random draw is keyed by (seed, purpose, frame, entity) (SPEC 3.7).
  - Match seeds are 5001–5010 (SPEC 3.7 seed registry).
  - Each open-play passage and each hero gets its own scenario seed, keyed off the match seed,
    at least 1,000,000. None is a design, evaluation or demo seed.
- **Rebuilding it.** The same seeds give byte-identical files and archive on the same platform
  and library versions. Across platforms, last-bit differences in numpy can grow (SPEC 3.7).

  ```bash
  uv run python -m sim.dataset --matches 10 --out out/dataset/
  ```

- **Parameters from published papers.** No parameter was fitted to real match data.

  | What | Value | Source |
  |---|---|---|
  | Field of view and occlusion | 120° binocular cone, Gaussian falloff with angle and distance, narrower at speed; occluders block soft angular sectors | Bekkers (2026), *Wide Open Gazes*, arXiv:2602.18519 |
  | Scan rate by role, and under pressure | fitted to ≈ 3 scans in the 10 s before receiving and to the role effect sizes; the rate falls to 0.61× with an opponent within 1 m | Jordet et al. (2020), Frontiers in Psychology 11:553813 |
  | Scan duration | lognormal dwell, fitted so that 90% of scans keep the ball out of an 82° frame ≤ 0.66 s | Aksum et al. (2021), PLoS ONE 16(8):e0244118 |
  | Scan head speed | peak 404 ± 51°/s | Kokubu et al. (2026), Frontiers in Psychology 17:1785026 |
  | Pressing intensity (`pressure` spells) | time-to-intercept based, 1.5 s threshold | Bekkers (2025), *Pressing Intensity*, arXiv:2501.04712 |
  | Time to intercept (decisions, pressing) | reaction 0.7 s, then 5 m/s | Spearman (2018), *Beyond Expected Goals* |
  | Shot speed | U(24, 30) m/s, within the 18–35 m/s of maximal instep kicks | Kellis & Katis (2007), J. Sports Science and Medicine 6(2) |
  | Save model | reach and save probability fitted on real penalties (a preprint) | Bransen, Janssen & Davis (2025), arXiv:2505.24629 |
  | Decision sampling | Gumbel-max with keyed noise | Oberst & Sontag (2019) |

- **Our own settings.** These are *tunable* choices, not fitted to anything:
  - movement limits: 7.0–9.5 m/s by role, 3.5 m/s² acceleration, 5 m/s² deceleration (none of
    the papers prints measured values);
  - ground-pass speeds;
  - in open play: the hold time, the pass rule and the marking distances;
  - the shot's aim error and the keeper's dive speed (SPEC 3.3).

  Full list and how far each source was read: [docs/REFERENCES.md](https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes/blob/main/docs/REFERENCES.md).
- **Comparisons.** How the sim's statistics compare with values printed in those papers:
  [eval/reports/realism.md](https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes/blob/main/eval/reports/realism.md)
  and [eval/reports/match_stats.md](https://github.com/timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes/blob/main/eval/reports/match_stats.md).
- **Processing.** None beyond quantisation, as listed under Conventions. The `pressure` and
  `restart` rows and the `receptions` summaries are computed by `sim/dataset.py` from the sim's
  output, as described above.

## Known limitations

The simulator simplifies football heavily. Read the data as the output of these rules.

- **No aerial play.** Every pass and shot travels along the ground. There are no crosses,
  headers or lofted balls; the ball's height is constant.
- **Possession-based stitching.** A match is separate possessions placed back to back, not 90
  minutes of continuous play.
  - Positions jump at every stitch, and beliefs reset there.
  - A restart's `kind` describes how the previous possession stopped. The next possession is not
    a simulated restart.
  - 18 of 19 possessions start with the home team on the ball. Only the corner (`corner_blind_side`)
    starts with the away team. So the home team has most of the ball, and a throw-in "won" by
    the away team can be followed by a home possession.
  - About 12.5 min of play per match, not 90.
- **Open play is a rule, not a decision.** In `possession_play` the carrier holds the ball for
  0.6–1.6 s, then passes to a teammate 8–35 m away. The teammate is picked by how much space he
  has on the true state, with random jitter.
  - There are no shots, dribbles or tackles in open play. The ball changes hands only by
    interception or going out.
  - Open play is pass-heavy. `eval/reports/match_stats.md` counts about 1,853 passes per
    90 min of play. No published target is configured to check that against (SPEC 3,
    acceptance checks).
- **Scripted heroes.** The four hero scenarios set up a situation with scripted passes and, for
  three of them, a scripted key scan. Their outcomes are designed:
  - the shot hero scores in 9 of 10 matches, which is not a realistic conversion rate;
  - the only tackle is in `press_escape`.
- **Same players, fixed shape.** The same 22 players with fixed formations play every match, and
  role parameters are shared within a role. There is no per-player trait, fatigue,
  substitution, foul, card or offside.
- **Perception model.** Vision is a cone with soft edges and occlusion. Beliefs are the last
  sighting, extrapolated at most 1 s, with no uncertainty stored. Real players also use memory,
  prediction and peripheral cues that are not modelled.
- **Decisions.** Only the hero carriers decide, valuing options with a smooth expected-threat
  prior. Receiver body orientation is not in the model.
- **Pressure spells** are thresholded from a continuous measure, and many are a single frame
  (§ `events`).
- **Reproducibility.** Byte identity holds only on the same platform and library versions.

## Uses

- **Fit for:**
  - testing and teaching tracking and event-data pipelines;
  - benchmarking scan detection from head yaw against ground-truth scans (as
    `eval/scan_detector.py` does);
  - developing vision, pressing and belief metrics against the sim's known beliefs;
  - prototyping visualisations;
  - reproducible demos.
- **Not fit for — it is not real football:**
  - any conclusion about real players, teams or tactics;
  - player evaluation, scouting or betting;
  - estimating real rates (passes, scans, shots, conversion);
  - training a model meant for real data without validating it on real data.

  Any effect measured here is causal only inside the sim. Its scanning, perception and decision
  parameters come from published papers, but its rules are ours.
- **Misuse to avoid.** Do not present the data as real, or attach real names, clubs or branding
  to it.

## Distribution

- **Where.** The archive is meant to be attached to a GitHub release of the repository. The
  repository holds only the generator and the one-possession sample.
- **Publishing is Bowen's call.** After this is merged, from an up-to-date `main`:

  ```bash
  uv run python -m sim.dataset --matches 10 --out out/dataset/
  ```

  ```bash
  gh release create dataset-v1 out/through-their-eyes-synthetic-matches-v1.tar.gz --repo timothyzhbw-jpg/through-their-eyes --target main --title "Synthetic match dataset v1" --notes "10 stitched synthetic matches from sim/dataset.py (fictional teams and players, not real football data): events, 25 Hz tracking, perception and decisions. Datasheet: docs/DATASET.md. SHA-256: $(shasum -a 256 out/through-their-eyes-synthetic-matches-v1.tar.gz | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  ```

- **Archive layout.** `through-their-eyes-synthetic-matches-v1/`, holding `DATASHEET.md` (this
  file), `manifest.json`, `metadata.json` and the tables. Each table is in Parquet; `events`,
  `receptions` and `decisions` are also in CSV.

## Maintenance

- **Maintainer.** Through Their Eyes; open an issue on the repository.
- **Versions.** A new version bumps `sim.dataset.VERSION`, keeps the match-seed registry and
  notes what changed here. Schema changes are additive within a version.
